title: `font-weight: calc(2000)` minifies to `2000`, a value outside the property's range that the browser drops
impact: No reactions (batch report). Out-of-range calc() in font-weight is a spec-precise edge case. Real stylesheets use keywords or 100-900 literals, and var()-based tokens are unparsed and unaffected. The follow-up comment's case is somewhat more plausible: an invalid literal (0, 1001, 9000) is accepted as typed and can override an earlier valid weight (`font-weight:bold;font-weight:9000` -> `font-weight:9000`, so the browser uses 400, not 700) or be folded into a `font` shorthand that the browser then drops whole (font-size and family too). That is still invalid input, but strict mode should reject it, and errorRecovery should keep it as written without discarding the valid fallback.
code: src/values/number.rs: NumericRange (All, NonNegative only) and CSSNumber::parse_with_range
summary: font-weight is `<number [1,1000]>`. lightningcss parses it as an unrestricted CSSNumber: calc() folds to its unclamped value, so `calc(2000)` (valid, clamped to 1000 by the browser) becomes the invalid literal `2000`; out-of-range literals are also accepted. Calcs should clamp to [1,1000], and out-of-range literals should fail to parse (falling back to unparsed, like `width:-5px` after #1329).
evidence: repro.mjs --all: same output on every release 1.14.0 through 1.33.0 and master (long-standing, not a regression). Chromium 153: computed weight for calc(2000) = 1000, calc(-5) = 1, calc(1000 + 1) = 1000; literals 2000/-5/0/0.5 and `font:9000 10px serif` are invalid (parse() = ''). equivalence.mjs: NOT EQUIVALENT (.b 700 -> 400, .c 1000 -> 400). Spec: css-fonts-4 `<font-weight-absolute> = [ normal | bold | <number [1,1000]> ]`, "Only values greater than or equal to 1, and less than or equal to 1000, are valid, and all other values are invalid." css-values-4: numeric functions "returning out-of-range values never cause a declaration to become invalid. Instead, the value ... is clamped to the range allowed in the context".

fix.approach: Parse AbsoluteFontWeight::Weight with a [1,1000] range: clamp folded calc() results and reject out-of-range literals so they fall back to unparsed. Either add a range variant to NumericRange (it is a public enum without #[non_exhaustive], so a new variant is technically a Rust API break) or write a custom Parse for AbsoluteFontWeight. Same type is used by the @font-face font-weight descriptor, which has the same range. Tests next to the existing font-weight tests. A candidate good first issue once the maintainer picks the approach.

notVerified: Only Chromium checked. Did not check the @font-face descriptor output or font-stretch/font-style oblique angle ranges, which may have the same class of bug.
